evals.prompt: Please create a PR from my clean tracked v0.10.2/service-update branch. It has three commits changing a validator, its tests, and unrelated contributor guidance. The branch already tracks origin/v0.10.2/service-update, but my latest local commits are not pushed yet. Do not treat this as approval to write remotely.
evals.expected_output: Collects the complete three-dot comparison, maps every changed path to reviewer themes, proposes V0.10.2/service update, and stops after the full CREATE preview before push or PR write.
expectations: Title is V0.10.2/service update
All commits, bodies, final patches, statuses, and paths are inspected
Validator behavior and contributor guidance are summarized as reviewer themes rather than a file list
The previewed body uses a short opening summary plus concise thematic sections
Preview names repo, base/head, title, body summary, counts, authenticated assignee, push, and exact writes
No push or PR write occurs without approval

evals.prompt: Create the pull request. I approve the exact plan you just showed. The local HEAD and remote state are unchanged.
evals.expected_output: Rechecks the approved snapshot, performs only the previewed normal push, create/edit, and assignment, then verifies the persisted PR and full file inventory.
expectations: Approval is applied to the same prepared plan without asking again
Tracked local commits missing from the remote branch are pushed normally before PR creation or update
Remote SHA equals local HEAD before PR metadata write
No reviewers, labels, milestones, projects, auto-merge, or unrelated writes
Post-write verification checks base, head, title, body, draft state, assignee, SHA, and all changed files

evals.prompt: Create a PR yolo from v12.0.2/chore-work. There is a clean branch and no existing PR.
evals.expected_output: Displays the CREATE mutation preview, then performs the permitted writes without a second confirmation; the title is V12.0.2/chore work.
expectations: The full preview is visible before remote mutations
Same-request yolo removes only the approval wait
No force push or history rewrite
The PR is ready for review unless draft was explicitly requested
Authenticated GitHub identity is used for assignment, not git user.name

evals.expected_output: Does not invoke a PR workflow or mutate a remote because no explicit PR request is attached.
expectations: Bare auto or yolo does not route to git-remote-pr
No remote read or write is initiated for a PR

evals.prompt: Please make a PR yolo. There is one modified tracked file and one new untracked file in my worktree.
evals.expected_output: Stops on the dirty worktree, explains that the uncommitted and untracked files cannot be represented by the PR, and leaves the worktree untouched.
expectations: Tracked modification blocks
Untracked file also blocks
No stage, commit, stash, discard, automatic commit skill, push, or PR write
Yolo does not bypass the gate

evals.prompt: Open a pull request from this checkout. Test detached HEAD, then a feature branch with no upstream configured, then the default branch, then a feature branch with an empty base...head comparison.
evals.expected_output: Each invalid state fails before any remote write with a distinct actionable diagnosis.
expectations: Detached HEAD blocks
Missing upstream tracking blocks
Current default/base branch blocks
Empty comparison blocks
No PR is created

evals.prompt: Create a PR yolo, but the existing remote head has an unrelated commit and a normal push would be non-fast-forward.
evals.expected_output: Reports divergence and stops without force pushing, rebasing, resetting, or opening a PR.
expectations: Remote head ancestry is checked before writes
Non-fast-forward state fails closed
No force push, rebase, reset, or merge
Yolo does not relax divergence handling

evals.prompt: Refresh the already-open PR for my branch. I added commits since its description was written. One early commit claimed a feature that a later commit reverted; a binary file and a rename are also in the final comparison.
evals.expected_output: Finds the existing head/base PR, regenerates the whole description from the current final diff into concise reviewer themes, accounts for all files, previews full-body replacement, and updates the same PR after approval.
expectations: Existing PR is UPDATE rather than duplicate CREATE
New commits and final patches determine the current description
Reverted behavior is not claimed even if earlier commits said otherwise
Binary and rename remain explicit evidence entries even when the prose stays concise
Whole-body replacement policy is previewed
Persisted body is checked exactly against the new body

evals.prompt: Create the pull request. The existing open PR already has the generated title and complete current body, its branch SHA is current, and I am assigned.
evals.expected_output: Verifies the existing PR and reports already up to date without a pointless metadata write.
expectations: Matching existing PR is reused
Complete changeset is still re-read
No metadata write when title, body, assignment, and head already match
Post-write style verification is performed

evals.prompt: I approved the PR preview, but before you execute I made another commit, changed the working tree, and the base branch moved.
evals.expected_output: Invalidates the old approval, prepares fresh evidence and a new preview, and asks again in normal mode without pushing or editing the PR.
expectations: Material state is rechecked immediately before writes
Dirty worktree independently blocks
Old approval is not reused
No remote mutation occurs from the invalidated plan

evals.prompt: Make a PR for a repository with a default PR template containing summary, related issue, validation, and unchecked checkboxes. The branch diff changes code and tests but no test command has run and no issue was linked.
evals.expected_output: Uses the repository template, fills supported change details with concise reviewer-oriented synthesis, leaves unsupported boxes unchecked, and invents no test result or issue relationship.
expectations: Repository default template wins over fallback layout
Required headings and checklist structure remain
Template headings are filled with concise thematic content instead of an appended fallback inventory
No unsupported checklist item is checked
No invented test run, CI result, or Closes/Fixes/Resolves keyword
No diffhunk links or AI attribution

evals.prompt: Create a PR yolo for a large branch with several unrelated change areas, generated files, deletions, and a patch-unavailable binary. The branch shape is similar to a release-sized skill PR: one new skill with scripts/evals/tests, broad repository guidance changes, documentation/catalog updates, validation work, and supporting assets. Verify that the GitHub PR files API returns a different file set than local base...head.
evals.expected_output: Groups the body into a short opening summary plus a small number of coarse reviewer themes while accounting for every local path; post-write verification reports the mismatched GitHub inventory and does not claim success.
expectations: Every path has an internal coverage theme even when many files collapse into shared reviewer sections
The body uses a concise opening summary and a small number of coarse reviewer themes for this large PR
Mechanical/generated, asset, reference, and binary entries are summarized honestly rather than surfaced as individual file bullets
No duplicate final Changes Summary repeats the thematic body
GitHub files API is paginated
Mismatch blocks success and reports any already-created PR URL
No fabricated behavior or validation claims

evals.prompt: Create a PR from a fork to its canonical parent. The authenticated GitHub login differs from git user.name. Simulate missing gh, missing authentication, then insufficient assignment permission in separate attempts.
evals.expected_output: Resolves the fork head and canonical base when unambiguous, uses the authenticated login, and fails each missing prerequisite before mutation with an actionable message.
expectations: Explicit repo/base/head are used for creation
No default main assumption or broad fetch
Assignee comes from gh authenticated user API
Missing gh and missing auth fail before mutation
Assignment eligibility failure is reported before mutation
Scratch artifacts stay outside the working tree

evals.prompt: Create a PR yolo, but the remote accepted the PR body with altered text and rejected assignment despite preflight. Test each failure separately.
evals.expected_output: Reports the PR URL and the specific persistence or assignment failure instead of claiming full success.
expectations: Complete body persistence is verified
Authenticated requester assignment is verified
Partial success identifies the existing PR URL
No extra metadata is modified to recover silently

evals.prompt: Open a pull request after I renamed my local branch from v0.10.2/service-update to v0.11.0/chore-and-git-remote-pr, but its upstream still points at origin/v0.10.2/service-update.
evals.expected_output: Fails before evidence collection, names the local/upstream mismatch explicitly, explains that stale tracking would target the wrong remote branch, and tells me how to update the remote branch name and upstream before retrying.
expectations: Local and upstream branch names are both shown
The mismatch is treated as stale tracking or an incomplete rename
Guidance includes updating upstream tracking after the remote branch name is corrected
No push, PR write, or silent recovery is attempted

evals.prompt: Refresh the PR for a branch comparable to codebeltnet/agentic#44: it adds one new skill with scripts, evals, and tests; restructures another skill with many reference changes; normalizes markdown across a large set of skills and scaffold templates; updates the README catalog and release notes; extends deterministic validation; and adds a handful of hero assets. The current generated body is accurate but bloated into a file-by-file inventory. Replace it with the current final-diff summary.
evals.expected_output: Keeps full internal coverage but rewrites the body into a concise reviewer-facing structure: short opening paragraph, a few bold themes, concise bullets, and no trailing inventory summary.
expectations: Complete changed-file coverage is maintained internally even though many files collapse into shared themes
The opening paragraph explains the purpose and major outcome before the thematic sections
Themes are coarse reviewer-facing categories rather than per-directory or per-file labels
Related skill docs, references, evals, assets, README, and validation changes are collapsed into shared themes when they support the same outcome
Mechanical or supporting changes are summarized rather than enumerated one file at a time
Paths, scripts, or identifiers appear only when they materially help the reviewer
No duplicate final Changes Summary or commit-log restatement appears after the thematic body
